nodes.label: B1: consoleAuth-only admin operations
nodes.rationale: API keys stay server-only, never in a browser; agency toggling its own plan flags would be self-granting features (D-096).

nodes.label: B2: no POST /api/v1/agencies
nodes.rationale: A platform-minted Agency would fight the CRM's own record on sourceUpdatedAt under last-writer-wins; the CRM's first trip/traveller push creates the Agency instead.

nodes.label: B3: platformAdminAuth-only partner bootstrap
nodes.rationale: Kaafil's own ops team provisioning a new customer is a different actor entirely, not something a partner self-serves.

nodes.label: B4: reviews and support tickets deferred (D-025)
nodes.rationale: For v1 a post-trip complaint is the CRM's to handle — a deliberate hand-off, not a gap nobody noticed (D-025).

nodes.label: B5: KaafilClient holds tokens in memory only
nodes.rationale: A half-durable store is worse than an absent one; the host app is expected to own persistence.

nodes.label: B6: no auth.revoke() method
nodes.rationale: The vendored spec's Auth tag has no revoke operation to wrap; the internal doc listing one is stale against the contract.

nodes.label: B7: no apiKeyAuth trip-listing operation
nodes.rationale: A CRM tracks its own trip refs via externalTripId rather than asking Kaafil to enumerate them back.

nodes.label: B8: no operation reads/lists a Manager entity
nodes.rationale: A CRM already holds the externalManagerId it upserted with; there is no server-side directory to page through.

nodes.label: B9: agency settings endpoints are consoleAuth
nodes.rationale: getAgencySettings/patchAgencySettings now exist but as consoleAuth — the same human-in-the-loop shape as B1, moved from §3 gap to §2 boundary; architecture/14-configuration.md §5 is the doc that is wrong.

nodes.label: sync-push-share-unauthenticated (P0, engine-side)
nodes.rationale: POST /api/v1/sync/push/share declares no security scheme at all; CredentialResolver correctly reads that as public, so kaafil-js refuses the call locally rather than sending a traveller's queued forms unauthenticated. Fix is engine-side: declare shareAuth on the route.

nodes.label: no-offline-outbox (CLOSED 2026-08-16, Phase 15)
nodes.rationale: A 409 never auto-merges by design; an absent pull section writes nothing, never treated as an empty list.

nodes.label: closing-day-unbuilt (CLOSED 2026-08-16, Phase 14)
nodes.rationale: unlockCloseout is apiKeyAuth only by design — the person who locks a trip is not the person allowed to reopen it.

nodes.label: dsar-erasure-export-unbuilt (CLOSED 2026-08-20)
nodes.rationale: Erasure anonymizes in place and is idempotent on erasedAt; export is generated fresh on every call, never a cached snapshot.

nodes.label: agency-admin-upsert-no-sdk-method (CLOSED 2026-08-20)
nodes.rationale: The raw-REST workaround this row documented is now a rule violation per CLAUDE.md R4, not a workaround.

nodes.label: usage-ingest-log-doc-mismatch (P1, doc gap)
nodes.rationale: readUsage/readIngestLog are security: [consoleAuth] in the shipped contract, contradicting architecture/13-operations.md §4.2's claim of API-key auth — the doc is the thing that is wrong.

nodes.label: comms-email-has-no-address (unscheduled)
nodes.rationale: Neither Traveller nor Manager carries an email column, so every EMAIL send falls through the channel-fallback walk as permanently unconfigured; reported rather than schema-patched to avoid unstated scope creep.

nodes.label: comms-entirely-ungated (unscheduled)
nodes.rationale: engagement-comms RULES R13 says comms is always-available, but the flag catalog is a closed 19-key set with no comms key — the gating it promises is unimplementable as written; opening that table is a commercial decision.

nodes.label: comms-no-production-sender (partly closed 2026-08-20)
nodes.rationale: The provider-credential vault shipped (createCommsProviderCredential seals a BYO key server-side); which adapters KAAFIL_SEND resolves outside dev is not observable from the vendored contract, so that half remains unverified.

nodes.label: History of the deleted 'raw' badge
nodes.rationale: raw existed to say 'the endpoint is live, the SDK just cannot reach it' — collapsing 'no SDK path' into 'no path' was a mistake this repo made once and corrected in writing.

nodes.label: npm dist-tag wrinkle: latest stuck on beta.0
nodes.rationale: npm always assigns the latest tag on a first-ever publish regardless of --tag; every publish since moved only the beta tag, so an unqualified npm install kaafil-js installs the older, buggier version.
